name: Speculative decoding batch dilution: why speedup collapses at production batch sizes
arithmetic_intensity: The core problem: speculative decoding raises arithmetic intensity from 1 to k on both passes, but a real decode step at batch B already has AI = B. So a k=4 speculative step at batch B has AI = B + k - the increment shrinks as a fraction of the total. At batch 1, speculative decoding converts AI from 1 to k (a kx improvement). At batch 32, it converts AI from 32 to 36 (only 12.5% improvement). At batch 128, from 128 to 132 (3.1%). This is why speculative decoding is a LATENCY optimization, not a THROUGHPUT optimization - the idle bandwidth it converts does not exist once B is large. The Medusa paper provides direct measured evidence: 'when the batch size exceeds 32, the speedup decreases and may even have a negative effect' because linear layers shift from memory-bandwidth-bound to compute-bound. EAGLE-3 paper confirms: in SGLang framework, EAGLE-3 achieves only 1.38x throughput improvement at batch size 64 (vs 3-6.5x at batch 1). This is the single most important practical caveat for production deployment.
scales_with: batch_size (the dominant term: relative benefit of raising AI from 1 to k shrinks as B grows)
draft_k (the AI increment; at large B the increment is negligible)
acceptance_rate (at large batch, even high acceptance cannot overcome the AI dilution)
draft_model_size (draft cost becomes pure overhead when verify is already compute-bound)
workarounds: Disable speculative decoding for throughput-oriented batches; enable only for latency-sensitive small-batch requests
Use n-gram/lookahead drafters at moderate batch sizes - zero draft cost means less overhead even when verify is compute-bound
Size decode pools in disaggregated serving to keep batch small
Adaptive draft_k - shorten the draft when acceptance rate drops (which happens naturally at large batch)
notes: Measured evidence: (1) Medusa paper Appendix G.3: simulated speedup for Llama-7B on A100 80GB PCIe shows speedup peaks at batch 1-16 and declines beyond batch 32, becoming negative at very high batch. (2) EAGLE-3 paper: 1.38x throughput at batch 64 in SGLang (vs 3-6.5x at batch 1). (3) The existing repo record speculative-decoding-bandwidth-trade-at-batch documents the AI math: at batch B, speculative step has AI = B+k vs B for normal decode, so the relative gain is k/B which → 0 as B → ∞. Production implication: speculative decoding should be treated as a latency optimization for small-batch requests, not a throughput optimization for large-batch serving. The batch size threshold where benefit disappears is hardware-dependent (higher on parts with more bandwidth headroom) but the qualitative behavior is universal.
